upsertPapers.title: Streaming and Massively Parallel Algorithms for Edge Coloring
Component Stability in Low-Space Massively Parallel Computation

upsertSlices.label: MPC; linear memory per machine
upsertSlices.task: Output explicit proper edge coloring in distributed memory
assumptions: Simple graph; input is an edge list distributed among machines
O(n) local memory and O(m) total memory, measured in words
Unlimited local computation in the MPC round model
No claim that Δ+Õ(Δ³ᐟ⁴) equals Δ+o(Δ) for bounded Δ

results.guarantee: Proper edge coloring using at most Δ+Õ(Δ³ᐟ⁴) colors
results.sourceLocation: Corollary 2, printed p. 15:4; Theorem 1 and Lemma 7
results.notes: The tilde hides factors depending on log n. Corollary 3 separately assumes Δ=n^Ω(1) and obtains sublinear local space with a different palette. That polynomial-degree regime is not the low-degree regime of the other panel.

upsertSlices.label: Low-space MPC · component stability
upsertSlices.task: Color edges in low-space MPC and understand conditional round limits
assumptions: Low-space MPC n^φ words per machine, fixed 0<φ<1
Upper: deterministic component-unstable, Δ=(log log n)^{o(1)}, n^{1+o(1)} total words, n^{poly(Δ)} local work
Lower: deterministic component-stable only, connectivity conjecture, even forests; polynomial global space allowed
Different exact palettes; no matched frontier

results.bound: O(poly(Δ)+log Δ · log log log n) rounds
results.guarantee: Proper edge coloring with palette Δ+√Δ·log³Δ
results.sourceLocation: Theorem 21 and proof; end of Section 4.2
results.notes: For sufficiently large fixed Δ, the palette is at most 2Δ−2 and the round bound is O(log log log n), with polynomial local computation. This is an asymptotic specialization, not a claim for every small fixed degree. No exponent is specified for poly(Δ).

results.guarantee: Lower bound for computing a proper (2Δ−2)-edge coloring
results.notes: The logarithm is log(log_Δ n), not log_Δ(log n). Component stability permits the global parameters allowed by the paper’s formal definition; it does not mean that machines cannot communicate across components. This is not a matched lower bound for Theorem 21.
